toolingGaps.status: diagnosed 2026-10-27. The Windows SDK IS installed (10.0.22621.0); rc.exe is not on PATH but the SDK is present. Three distinct problems, only the first of which was a host artifact.
findings: RESOLVED by the coordinator: a stale shared cargo target artifact at E:/build-cache/target/debug/build/trade-journal-desktop-119a88e22edbe3fa/out/resource.rc hardcoded the ICON path of the now-deleted Phase 01 worktree (codex-ai-native-journal-p01). rc.exe cannot read a file that no longer exists and reports it as 'RC2175 resource file is not in 3.00 format', which is a misleading message for a missing file. Clearing the stale trade-journal-desktop-* build dirs in the shared target removed the RC2175 entirely.

REPO DEFECT: desktop/scripts/run-sidecar-setup.js uses CommonJS require() while desktop/package.json declares type: module, so the repository's own 'pnpm --filter desktop setup:sidecar' fails with 'ReferenceError: require is not defined in ES module scope'. The sidecar binaries/node-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc.exe is therefore never produced, and cargo check then fails with "resource path binaries/node-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc.exe doesn't exist". Fix is a one-line import conversion.

REPO DEFECT: desktop/src-tauri/scripts/gen_icons/src/main.rs write_ico emits an invalid ICO despite its comment claiming Windows rc.exe compatibility. The generated icon.ico has ICONDIR type=0 (must be 1 for an icon), count=1 where six sizes were written, entry width=6 height=0, and entry size/offset values (73924640 / 6684672) that point far beyond the end of the 370072-byte file.
toolingGaps.impact: The root pnpm typecheck fails in the desktop workspace for reasons independent of the AI-native journal work: this is pre-existing on main and blocks the CI typecheck step and the G-FINAL whole-project gate. The per-phase gate is unaffected - web, core and importers typecheck all exit 0.
toolingGaps.decision: The coordinator diagnosed but did not fix the two repository defects: desktop tooling is outside the AI-native journal scope and is owned by the later operational phase. They need an explicitly scoped change, not silent scope creep.
toolingGaps.blocking: blocks the root pnpm typecheck element of the whole-project gate only

dispatchGuidance.raisedBy: user, 2026-10-26, after the Phase 01 and Phase 02 dispatches
dispatchGuidance.problem: Phase 01 burned about 3 hours in six plan-review rounds chasing wording defects and produced no code; the worker later said the plan was sound after round 2 and that the looping was its own wrong call. Phase 02 then spent 45+ minutes in a parallel reviewer-subagent round before its implementation commit and needed an active coordinator nudge to start working.
dispatchGuidance.mechanism: the repository pre-commit gate refuses any commit whose .omp/reviewer-report.md does not carry '## Verdict: PASS', so a worker that reviews a document before committing it can be trapped in an open-ended loop
rules: at most two reviewer runs for the whole phase: one on the plan, one on the implementation diff
wording, formatting and completeness nits are not findings; only a defect that changes runtime behaviour, file ownership or the contract is a finding
timebox the phase plan to about 30 minutes and commit it; the plan is a contract, not a document to perfect
never re-review a plan after a pass that produced only nits; record them as accepted deviations in the plan's design decisions instead
the reviewer verdict is produced from the implementation diff, not from iterating on prose

keep the dispatch brief to the delta: resolved runtime values, handoff facts and the few real traps, pointing at the committed packet for the contract instead of restating it, because restating the contract invites a clause-by-clause checking mode
the coordinator nudges the worker once when it appears to be idling, rather than letting it sit in a loop
dispatchGuidance.alsoLearned: the worker-read transcript source can serve a stale bounded window and make a live worker look hung; the terminal source is the reliable view of what the agent is actually doing
